name: Saint Christopher Magallanes and Companions
history: Twenty-five Mexican martyrs, twenty-two priests and three laymen, killed in the years when the public practice of the faith was restricted and priests were hunted, above all during the Cristero War of 1926 to 1929. Christopher Magallanes, a parish priest of Jalisco, was shot in 1927 after forgiving his executioners. John Paul II canonised them in 2000.
life: Cristóbal Magallanes Jara was born in 1869 at Totatiche in Jalisco and worked the land before entering the seminary. As parish priest of his home town he built schools, founded a seminary, and cared for the poor and for the native Huichol people. When the laws of the 1920s closed churches and forbade priests to minister, he kept serving his people in secret and reopened his seminary in hiding. He wrote against taking up arms, though many Catholics had joined the Cristero rising. On 21 May 1927 he was arrested on his way to celebrate Mass, and four days later he was shot at Colotlán without trial, together with his young assistant, Saint Agustín Caloca. He gave away his last possessions to the soldiers, absolved them, and prayed that his blood might bring peace to Mexico. His companions were priests and laymen from several dioceses who died in similar ways.
prayerTo: Saint Christopher Magallanes and holy martyrs of Mexico, you served Christ’s people when it was forbidden and forgave those who killed you. Pray for the Church in Mexico and wherever priests are persecuted. Give me courage to keep the faith in hidden ways when I cannot keep it openly, and a heart that forgives. Amen.
penance: Pray for priests who serve in danger, and for persecutors. Forgive someone today, in your heart at least, as the martyrs forgave their executioners.
meditation: He gave his executioners his blessing and what little he had. What would it take for you to bless someone who has harmed you?
